prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and of its bioactive form, which made incretin-based therapies for type 2 diabetes and obesity possible

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: a single-part prize for B010 with Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. The chair is right that six matching ballots are not an argument, so I restate the scientific basis. This is one discovery arc with a clear conceptual change: a gut hormone axis controlling insulin, glucagon, gastric emptying and appetite was established in humans, the bioactive truncated peptide was defined, the receptor biology and therapeutic rationale were worked out, and the result was confirmed by large independent randomized trials in glycaemia, weight, and cardiovascular and renal outcomes. That is the kind of specific, field-changing discovery I look for, and maturity is not in question; the effect has been replicated for years by many groups. The three names cover the physiological, molecular and translational-bridge core. I would keep the citation on the physiology and bioactive peptide while saying explicitly that this work made the therapies possible, so that it does not read as rewarding the hormone while ignoring the drugs.
statement.case_against: The attribution risk is real and I have not reduced it since round 1. Priority between Mojsov and the Habener group for the bioactive GLP-1(7-36) peptide rests on recollection, and nobody on this committee, myself included, has checked it against primary papers and dates in this record. Habener is not among the credited names on the ballot, so we cannot substitute him here. Knudsen, who is credited, is left out only because of the three-person cap, and that cut is a committee choice, not a finding about her contribution. Long-term obesity outcome and safety data are still accumulating, though I now treat that as secondary to the discovery. If a documentary check showed Mojsov's contribution to be derivative, this configuration would need to be reworked, and I would then take Knudsen's claim seriously as first reserve.

responses.point: The chair proposes Knudsen as first reserve if the attribution review weakens any of the three names, and declines to displace a discoverer now.
responses.response: I agree with this ordering and I accept it as my own. The physiological principle that justified long-acting agonists came from the discoverers, so the cap should settle the present allocation. But reserve status should be explicit: if the Mojsov check fails, the choice is between Knudsen and a different configuration, not a quiet substitution. I also hold to my round-1 reservation on B020 that you quoted: its medical relevance is conceptual and disease-associated and not yet an intervention. I keep it only as an alternative, and I accept your reading that it is tidier on attribution than anything else on the list.

responses.point: Sandberg says Mojsov's inclusion is better supported than adding an industrial name and wants the claim tested against the primary papers before the final ballot, and he asks what the fallback is if B010 fails.
responses.response: I agree that the primary papers should be consulted before we vote, and I would not treat my recall as settled. Our disagreement is small. You regard B006 and B020 as ahead of B008 in a fallback, and I do too. Where I would press you is that B020 is clean only for the Ire1 and HAC1/XBP1 core, with PERK and ATF6 outside the Walter and Mori pairing, so 'cleanest attribution' overstates it. If B010 failed, I would move to B006 first despite its attribution problem, since it has the clinical record that B020 lacks. I would not pair either with B010 now.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius supports B006 with June and Sadelain as the strongest competitor to B010 and doubts Rosenberg's place, since adoptive cell transfer is not CAR design.
responses.response: I now agree with narrowing to June and Sadelain on the science; Rosenberg's decisive contribution is adoptive cell transfer, and I withdraw my round-1 reluctance to reduce the names. The remaining defect is not a matter of numbers. Eshhar proposed the chimeric receptor concept and is outside the credited names on this ballot, so even a two-name B006 is open to the charge that it leaves out the origin of the idea. I therefore keep it as my first alternative and not as a second part alongside B010, and I would not call it ready until that gap can be defended.

responses.point: Linnarsson accepts the Knudsen exclusion as a consequence of the cap and would not word it as if industrial work counts for less.
responses.response: I agree, and I am glad we have settled the wording. I raised the consistency point about Bennett in B045 because we cannot exclude a developer here and then give the same weight to a developer elsewhere without saying why. It is separable in B010 because the physiology precedes the drug chemistry. B045 was not on any of our alternative lists, and I have not changed that, since I regard the antisense arc as early and exposed to being read as a prize for antisense technology generally. If the committee excludes Knudsen on the ground of the cap, I would want the same logic stated for B045.

responses.point: El-Manira prefers a single settled GLP-1 prize to a two-part configuration that adds B006 or B008, and notes that both alternatives carry serious attribution problems.
responses.response: I agree with the conclusion, and I accept your correction that my round-1 contrast between B006 and B008 on medical grounds was too neat. CAR-T has the clearer clinical record, but your point that the Eshhar omission makes its attribution as fragile as optogenetics holds. Where I still differ is on kind: the channelrhodopsin discovery is a real discovery, but the neuronal deployment is method development with limited clinical reach, so for this prize I would put B008 behind B006 and B020. That is a judgement about readiness and not about the quality of the work, and for that reason I do not support a two-part prize.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov's identification and synthesis of the bioactive GLP-1(7-36) peptide can be separated from the Habener group's work; this needs primary papers and dates that none of us has checked.
Whether the committee would proceed with the three-name allocation if priority remains unsettled, given that Habener is not on the ballot.
Whether the citation should name the therapies, which would reopen Knudsen's claim at the cost of Mojsov or Drucker.
Whether any CAR-T configuration is defensible without Eshhar, which determines whether B006 is a usable fallback.
How the committee should weigh accumulating long-term obesity outcome and safety data.
statement.conflict_note: No change. I report no collaboration with, or involvement in, any credited name on the shortlist. My nuclear-receptor and dopamine-neuron work does not overlap with these discoveries. I note co-authorship with El-Manira (2009) and Svenningsson, as disclosed in round 1, and I do not regard these as relevant to any shortlisted ballot. I do not infer other ties from shared institutions.
